newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's GAZ 1996 net profit 48.1 bln rbls.
newsitem.headline: Russia's GAZ 1996 net profit 48.1 bln rbls.

text.p: NOTES -- Full name AO Gorkovsky Avtomobilny Zavod (GAZ).
Alexei Gorynin, head of GAZ's property department, told Reuters the fall in pre-tax profit reflected the sharp increase in production costs.

He said a representative of shareholder Bank Menatep, Alexei Golubovich, had been voted onto the board of directors at the annual shareholder's meeting on Saturday, as well as a representative of investment fund EEDF, set up by British financial firm INVESCO.
Menatep owns 8.02 percent of GAZ's shares, and EEDF holds 7.8 percent, Gorynin said. Avtobank holds 10 percent.
GAZ appointed KPMG to prepare an audit of its accounts to international standards.

These figures are not prepared to international accounting standards but to Russian accounting standards on an accruals basis. Russian accounts are designed to meet the requirements of the tax authorities. Russian companies can choose whether to show revenues and spending on a cash or accruals basis. Definitions of profit and assets differ significantly from those in the West, and converting Russian accounts to international standards can turn a profit into a loss.
Figures are not adjusted for inflation or the depreciation of the rouble, but the following data may be helpful.
